A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VISTA, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The earlier experimental Appendix C is retained as Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, industrial ablations, online A/B results, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds reconstruction-loss learning curves and further deployment results.

M1.justification: The two-stage architecture, quasi-linear attention, reconstruction objective, and cached inference procedure remain unchanged. The new reconstruction discussion and refresh cadence document existing components without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use Amazon-Electronics, KuaiRand-1K, Minimal Production, and industrial production data for the same recommendation tasks. The added analyses use existing coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C adds VISTA without reconstruction loss as a comparator in the Amazon experiment; v1 reported this ablation only for industrial data in Table 3. The external baseline set—DIN, TTSN, MHA, SASRec, and HSTU—remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Amazon analysis compares reconstruction-loss inclusion versus omission using training-step curves and final evaluation reconstruction error. Section 4 also reports a cached-versus-direct online comparison. Existing splits, hyperparameters, and the 15-day, 5%-traffic A/B protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Figure 11 examine how the reconstruction objective affects reconstruction quality and convergence on Amazon, supplementing the existing industrial ablation. Section 4 adds a reported check that two-hour cached embeddings perform similarly to direct summarization.

E5.justification: A new Table 2 footnote reports paired t-tests and ANOVA comparisons at p < 0.001. Both versions already report results across three seeds with uncertainty values; v2 does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises VISTA-w/o-QLA on Minimal Production: AUC changes from 0.628 ± 0.014 to 0.627 ± 0.016, and NE from 1.024 ± 0.03 to 1.038 ± 0.05. v2 additionally reports reconstruction-related gains of 0.22% AUC and 1.11% NE, similar performance with two-hour cached embeddings, and a 94% inference GPU-resource reduction. Other benchmark results and existing result plots are retained.

T1.justification: The attention and reconstruction-loss equations and Appendix B's forward/backward derivations are unchanged. New Appendix C supplies empirical analysis and explanation, not new mathematical definitions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: two-stage cached attention, quasi-linear attention, reconstruction loss, and industrial deployment. New results support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C presents reconstruction error as a quantitative proxy for information retained in virtual embeddings and interprets explicit reconstruction optimization as improving convergence beyond the plateau seen without it. Existing applicability and storage-cost discussions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly specifies that summarization embeddings refresh every two hours. This is additional deployment information, not evidence of a changed cadence. Existing hyperparameters, implementation descriptions, and resource links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Liu et al. (2023), Deep Group Interest Modeling of Full Lifelong User Behaviors for CTR Prediction, and briefly describes its grouped-history attention. Consolidating the duplicate Katharopoulos references does not remove a distinct prior work.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a short reconstruction appendix, renumbers the experimental appendix, fixes the unresolved Figure 4 reference and several typos, and updates author, acknowledgment, and conference-header text. Most prose and the narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the reconstruction-loss plot as Figure 11 and a significance footnote to Table 2. Figure 6, Tables 3–4, and appendix figures are relocated or reflowed; subsequent figures are renumbered. Existing architecture and result graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The added reconstruction analysis provides targeted evidence for an existing objective, while the refresh cadence and reported GPU savings make deployment behavior more concrete. Reference and wording corrections also improve clarity. These are limited gains: most evidence is unchanged, and the new significance tests are only briefly specified.
